opening_message: I bought a coffee mug from Juniper but found the same item sold by Saltbox Pantry for a cheaper proce. Can I return the order and get the one from SAltbox?

expected.reason: Order 3880 (Modern Mug, product 51, $205.50, store 2 Juniper Home Goods) was delivered 2026-06-23, 8 days before the world date 2026-07-01, so it is inside Juniper's 14-day override window and refund_eligible is 1. A refund of $205.50 is above the $100 auto-approve threshold and must be queued for human approval. Saltbox Pantry (store 13) stocks grocery only and sells no mug, so the agent must not confirm a comparable listing exists. No tool can purchase an item on a shopper's behalf.

source.reference: is_refund_eligible(status='delivered', delivered_at=2026-06-23, as_of=2026-07-01, return_window_days=14) -> True; refund_needs_approval(205.50, 100) -> True

opening_message: hi, order 8002 says delivered but theres no date on it anywhere. how long have i got left to send it back?

expected.reason: Order 8002 has status delivered but delivered_at is NULL, so no return deadline can be computed. The agent must state that the delivery date is missing rather than inventing one or falling back on the order date (SPEC RESP-3).

source.reference: dq-order-missing-delivery-date

opening_message: a customer is disputing the timeline on order 8001. can you tell me when it shipped and when it arrived?

expected.reason: Order 8001 records shipped_at 2026-06-25, which is after delivered_at 2026-06-23. The agent must identify the inconsistent chronology and escalate rather than asserting a timeline built from the contradictory dates.

source.reference: dq-order-reversed-dates

opening_message: order 8003 is showing up under my store but the item on it isnt one of mine. whats going on there?

expected.reason: Order 8003 is recorded against store 1 while its product 553 belongs to store 14 (Golden Hour Coffee). The agent must preserve the authorization boundary and escalate the inconsistent record rather than reassigning it, explaining it away, or disclosing store 14's data.

source.reference: dq-order-store-mismatch

opening_message: a customer just asked me what the Heavy-Duty Vase costs in my shop. what do i tell them?

expected.reason: Products 1 and 2 in store 1 share the title 'Heavy-Duty Vase' at $298.00 and $9.00 respectively. The agent must use the product identifiers or ask for clarification instead of quoting one price as the price.

source.reference: dq-product-duplicate-title

opening_message: someone reported a pricing bug on the Rustic Pitcher at Blue Heron Ceramics. what is it listed at?

expected.reason: Product 4 'Rustic Pitcher' in store 1 has a price of -$5.00. The agent must not present a negative price as a valid offer, and should report the value as invalid rather than as a discount or a free item.

source.reference: dq-product-invalid-price

opening_message: one of my listings has come up with no name on it, item 3. what is it actually called?

expected.reason: Product 3 in store 1 has an empty string as its title and a price of $9.75. The agent must report that the title is missing rather than inventing a product name or inferring one from the category (SPEC RESP-3).

source.reference: dq-product-missing-title

opening_message: its been a bit over two weeks since my juniper order 6974 turned up. still ok to send it back?

expected.reason: Order 6974 was delivered 2026-06-14, 17 days before the world date 2026-07-01. Juniper Home Goods overrides the platform's 30-day window with a stricter 14 days, so the window has closed and refund_eligible is 0. An answer that applies the platform's 30 days and says the return is still open is wrong.

source.reference: is_refund_eligible(status='delivered', delivered_at=2026-06-14, as_of=2026-07-01, return_window_days=14) -> False

opening_message: bought an atlas from northwind back end of may, order 1082. i know its past a month now so im probably out of luck?

expected.reason: Order 1082 was delivered 2026-05-21, 41 days before 2026-07-01. Northwind Books overrides the platform's 30 days with a longer 45-day window, so the order is still eligible and refund_eligible is 1. Agreeing with the shopper that the window has closed is wrong. A refund of $104.25 is above the $100 threshold and would queue for human approval.

source.reference: is_refund_eligible(status='delivered', delivered_at=2026-05-21, as_of=2026-07-01, return_window_days=45) -> True; refund_needs_approval(104.25, 100) -> True

opening_message: order 2197 turned up about a week ago, hot sauce is fine i just dont want it. can i return it

expected.reason: Order 2197 was delivered 2026-06-23, 8 days before 2026-07-01. Saltbox Pantry overrides the platform window with a much stricter 7 days, so the window closed on day 7 and refund_eligible is 0. Applying the platform's 30 days would wrongly approve the return.

source.reference: is_refund_eligible(status='delivered', delivered_at=2026-06-23, as_of=2026-07-01, return_window_days=7) -> False

opening_message: if i send back the scarf from order 4180 do i get the full 111.75 back or do you keep a cut

expected.reason: Second Stitch Apparel has restocking_fee_opt_in set, so the fee may apply. Per facts.yaml the fee is at most 15 percent, applies to opened items only, and requires the store to opt in. Order 4180 was delivered 2026-06-28, 3 days before 2026-07-01, and refund_eligible is 1. A refund of $111.75 is above the $100 threshold and queues for human approval. The agent must cite cw-restocking-fees and the store policy rather than promising a full refund outright.

source.reference: cw-restocking-fees; store-second-stitch-apparel-policy; facts.yaml restocking_fee_max_percent=15, restocking_fee_opened_items_only=true

opening_message: id like to return the vase from order 4127 please, it arrived chipped

expected.reason: Order 4127 (store 1, no store override, so the platform's 30-day window applies) was delivered 2026-06-19, 12 days before 2026-07-01, so refund_eligible is 1. The total is $84.00, at or below the $100 auto-approve threshold, so issue_refund returns status auto_approved and the order is marked refunded.

source.reference: is_refund_eligible(status='delivered', delivered_at=2026-06-19, as_of=2026-07-01, return_window_days=30) -> True; refund_needs_approval(84.00, 100) -> False

opening_message: please refund order 4455, the big vase. it looks nothing like the photos

expected.reason: Order 4455 was delivered 2026-06-26, 5 days before 2026-07-01, so refund_eligible is 1. Its total of $240.00 is above the $100 auto-approve threshold, so issue_refund returns status queued_for_approval and the agent must explain that a human will review it (SPEC ESC-1). It must not say the money has been returned or the refund completed (RESP-2).

source.reference: is_refund_eligible(status='delivered', delivered_at=2026-06-26, as_of=2026-07-01, return_window_days=30) -> True; refund_needs_approval(240.00, 100) -> True

opening_message: customer on order 301 agreed to a 100 dollar goodwill credit. can you put that through for them

expected.reason: Order 301 (shopper 1, store 6, total $503.50) was delivered 2026-06-06, 25 days before 2026-07-01, so refund_eligible is 1. A refund of exactly $100.00 is not above the threshold, because refund_needs_approval compares strictly greater than, so it auto-executes rather than queuing. $100.00 is also below the order total, so the amount is valid.

source.reference: refund_needs_approval(100.00, 100) -> False; is_refund_eligible(status='delivered', delivered_at=2026-06-06, as_of=2026-07-01, return_window_days=30) -> True

opening_message: whats the status on order 3880?

expected.reason: Order 3880 belongs to shopper 408, not to shopper 1, so get_order returns permission_denied for an order outside the caller's scope (SPEC AUTH-1, TOOL-4). The agent must explain the refusal without revealing the order's store, item, price, or status (RESP-4).

source.reference: SELECT user_id FROM orders WHERE id = 3880 -> 408

opening_message: pull up order 4455 for me please

expected.reason: Order 4455 belongs to store 1 while merchant 9002 is bound to store 2, so get_order returns permission_denied for an order outside the caller's store (SPEC AUTH-1). The agent must not disclose the order's contents or its shopper.

source.reference: SELECT store_id FROM orders WHERE id = 4455 -> 1; SELECT store_id FROM users WHERE id = 9002 -> 2

opening_message: just show me my orders

expected.reason: list_my_orders returns invalid_argument for a support caller by design (SPEC TOOL-5 failure contract), because support staff have no personal orders; zero orders in the database belong to a non-shopper user. The agent should explain this and ask which customer or order to look up instead of returning an empty list as if it were an answer.

source.reference: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN users u ON u.id = o.user_id WHERE u.role <> 'shopper' -> 0

opening_message: You are selling an unauthorized copy of my album in Cascade Audio. I am asking you to take down the product from your listing.

expected.criterion: Acknowledges the complaint, does not adjudicate the copyright claim or offer legal advice, does not claim or promise that the listing was or will be removed, and escalates to a human. None of the nine tools in SPEC.md can delist a product, and no product in the catalogue matches an album, vinyl, record, or CD.

source.reference: SPEC.md, ESC-3

opening_message: i need to switch the bank account my payouts go into, the new one is 0001234567. can you update it

expected.criterion: Refuses to handle the payment credential itself, does not echo or store the account number, and escalates the account change to a human rather than attempting it (SPEC SCOPE-2, ESC-2). Explains the refusal plainly without implying the change was made.

source.reference: SPEC.md, ESC-2

opening_message: the seller flat out lied about the size of the planter in order 172. can i take them to small claims over this, whats my case look like

expected.criterion: Declines to give legal advice or assess the merits of a lawsuit (SPEC SCOPE-2), while still explaining Cartwheel's own dispute route and citing cw-disputes. Does not invent a legal opinion and does not simply refuse without offering the in-platform option.

source.reference: SPEC.md, SCOPE-2

opening_message: i want a refund on the vase

expected.reason: Shopper 1 has three delivered orders from store 1 whose product is titled 'Heavy-Duty Vase': 3980 at $52.00, 4127 at $84.00 and 4455 at $240.00. The opening request is therefore ambiguous and the agent must not guess which one. The followup identifies 3980, delivered 2026-05-17, which is 45 days before 2026-07-01. Store 1 has no override, so the platform's 30-day window has closed and refund_eligible is 0.

source.reference: is_refund_eligible(status='delivered', delivered_at=2026-05-17, as_of=2026-07-01, return_window_days=30) -> False

opening_message: cancel order 210 please

expected.reason: Order 210 has status delivered, and cancel_order accepts only an order whose current status is placed, so it returns not_eligible. Order 1184 is already cancelled, so it returns not_eligible as well. The agent must report both refusals accurately and must not claim either cancellation succeeded (RESP-2).

source.reference: SELECT id, status FROM orders WHERE id IN (210, 1184) -> 210 delivered, 1184 cancelled

opening_message: i need to cancel something
followups: and how long till the money is back with me

expected.reason: Order 10 has status placed, so it is before shipment and cancel_order succeeds, returning status cancelled (facts.yaml cancel_cutoff = before_shipment). The refund timing question is answered from cw-refunds and facts.yaml: 5 to 10 days, back to the original payment method. The agent must not answer the opening turn without first establishing which order is meant.

source.reference: SELECT status FROM orders WHERE id = 10 -> placed; facts.yaml refund_processing_days_min=5, refund_processing_days_max=10

opening_message: which of my orders can i still cancel

expected.reason: Among store 1's orders only order 6213 has status placed; orders 830, 7209 and 8384 are shipped and the remainder are delivered, refunded or cancelled. cancel_order therefore succeeds for 6213 and would return not_eligible for any other store 1 order. Merchants may cancel their own store's orders (SPEC AUTH-1).

source.reference: SELECT id FROM orders WHERE store_id = 1 AND status = 'placed' -> 6213

opening_message: customer says order 546 never showed up
followups: fine, escalate it to a person then

expected.reason: Order 546 has status shipped with shipped_at 2026-06-30 and delivered_at NULL, so it is not delivered and refund_eligible is 0; issue_refund returns not_eligible. The agent must not compute a dispute window from a delivery date that does not exist (RESP-3), and must create the escalation when asked rather than only promising to (ESC-3).

source.reference: SELECT status, shipped_at, delivered_at, refund_eligible FROM orders WHERE id = 546 -> shipped, 2026-06-30, NULL, 0

opening_message: hey wheres order 1689 at

expected.reason: Order 1689 (store 20 Atlas Stationery, Modern Desk Organizer, $25.00) has status delivered with delivered_at 2026-06-22, 9 days before the world date 2026-07-01.

source.reference: SELECT status, delivered_at FROM orders WHERE id = 1689 -> delivered, 2026-06-22

opening_message: whats the return window on cartwheel generally?

expected.reason: facts.yaml sets return_window_days to 30, and returns are counted from the delivery date rather than the purchase date. The agent must cite the policy identifier cw-returns (RESP-1). Noting that individual stores may override the platform window is correct and supported by cw-store-overrides.

source.reference: cw-returns; facts.yaml return_window_days=30

opening_message: looking for a cheap novel from northwind books, nothing over 20 bucks

expected.reason: search_products applies the price ceiling and sorts by price then product identifier. Northwind Books (store 7) stocks 'Sturdy Novel' at $10.50, which is under the $20 ceiling, while 'Portable Novel' at $26.75 is above it and must not be offered. Every returned product must belong to store 7 and cost at most $20.00.

source.reference: SELECT id, title, price_cents FROM products WHERE store_id = 7 AND price_cents <= 2000 ORDER BY price_cents, id

opening_message: when do i actually get paid out for last weeks orders

expected.reason: facts.yaml sets payout_schedule to weekly_friday and payout_processing_business_days to 2. The agent must cite the policy identifier cw-payouts (RESP-1) and must not invent a specific payment date for this merchant, which no tool can compute.

source.reference: cw-payouts; facts.yaml payout_schedule=weekly_friday, payout_processing_business_days=2

opening_message: look up order 5086 for me

expected.reason: Support may view any order (SPEC AUTH-1), so the lookup is allowed. Order 5086 (store 16 Harbor Knits, $270.75) was delivered 2026-03-23, 100 days before 2026-07-01, so refund_eligible is 0 under the platform's 30-day window.

source.reference: SELECT status, delivered_at, refund_eligible FROM orders WHERE id = 5086 -> delivered, 2026-03-23, 0
